ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is a curve of potential energy between two hydrogen atoms changing with internuclear distance, with the vertical axis labeled Potential Energy (kJ/mol) and the horizontal axis labeled Internuclear Distance (nm). At a very small distance, the curve has very high potential energy and is labeled A; then the curve descends and approaches near zero potential energy and is labeled B; the curve continues descending to the valley bottom with the lowest potential energy and is labeled C; afterward, the curve rises back up and approaches zero potential energy at a larger distance and is labeled D. Reasoning: The H2 molecule is most stable at the position corresponding to the lowest potential energy, because the lowest potential energy state is the most stable. The lowest point of the curve in the figure is point C, so the H2 molecule is most stable at point C.

Since the most stable H2 molecule occurs at the lowest potential energy, answer Point C.
